title: Gentle-batcher throttle sprint summit notes
content:
Purpose: quick capture from the sprint summit focused on the "gentle-batcher" throttling experiments, kernel handshake changes to reduce tail latency, and KV cache eviction behaviour observed during bursty traffic. This is a working note — hypotheses, test results, and next steps.

Attendees: Maya C., Liam O'C., Priya N., Diego A., Sofia M., Paul R. (oncall drop-in)

High-level summary:
- Ran a 48-hour canary of the gentle-batcher smoothing window change (ramp-window=40ms -> 20ms) on canary cluster (c-canary-12).
- Observed p95 reduction ~6% for small-seq (<128) requests, p99 improvement ~3%, but slight p50 regression (~1.5%) during sustained burst spikes.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~2.7% under synthetic burst tests due to earlier eviction from deadtime trimming; ejection rate increased for long-lived contexts.
- Kernel handshake tweak (handshake-sleep=100us -> 40us) reduced handshake CPU syscalls but introduced jitter on one node (suspect NIC interrupt coalescing interplay).

Notes from standup-style check-ins:
- Maya: Summarized canary results and compiled traces; top affected route is /v1/chat (few-shot prompts) with heavy KV reuse. Root cause hypothesis: aggressive window trimming reduces batching overlap for warm requests and pushes some traffic into smaller batches.
- Liam: Did deeper profiling on the kernel side. Found an unexpected lock contention on kernel scheduler path when batch size > 32 and concurrent repopulation of KV cache occurs. Proposed micro-optim: bump per-thread freelist and change lock scope to per-eviction-queue.
- Priya: Validated end-to-end latency with and without the gentle-batcher on a production shadow fleet. She saw that when traffic contained >30% long-context queries, the gentle-batcher caused higher jitter for simultaneous short queries. Suggests better routing isolation for long-context classes.
- Diego: Noted the eviction delta — cache TTL trimming was configured to remove entries with deadtime>300s; we switched to 200s on canary. That lowered memory footprint but increased miss rate on certain flows. Diego recommends adding a cohort-based TTL (short/medium/long) rather than global.
- Sofia: Looked at kernel handshake jitter and NIC metrics. On node A1, interrupt coalescing increased effective latency under the new handshake timing. Suggested experimenting with handshake backoff tied to NIC load rather than fixed microseconds.

Experiment details (synth and prod-shadow):
- Canary period: 2027-03-09 14:00 -> 2027-03-11 14:00 UTC.
- Config delta: gentle-batcher.ramp_window_ms: 40 -> 20; kvcache.deadtime_trim_s: 300 -> 200; kernel.handshake_sleep_us: 100 -> 40.
- Traffic model: mixed 70% short (<64 tokens) / 20% medium / 10% long (>1024 tokens), plus 20% canary-only synthetic burst spikes at 2x baseline for 30s every 5 min.
- Observed metrics (summary averages across canary cluster):
  - p50 latency: baseline 18ms -> canary 18.3ms (regression +1.5%)
  - p95 latency: baseline 78ms -> canary 73.3ms (improvement -6%)
  - p99 latency: baseline 190ms -> canary 184.3ms (improvement -3%)
  - KV cache hit rate: baseline 83.5% -> canary 80.8% (drop -2.7%)
  - Eviction rate: baseline 0.9%/min -> canary 1.4%/min
  - CPU sys usage on kernel threads: baseline 48% -> canary 42%

Interpretation / hypotheses:
- Short-tail improvement indicates smoother batching for the majority of short requests; window trimming nudges more requests into better-packed batches at the cost of occasional starvation when bursts align with long-context eviction windows.
- KV cache hit rate drop likely due to the deadtime trimming being too aggressive for long-lived contexts (conversational sessions). We need a mixed TTL approach and smarter pinning for pinned keys (token caches for ongoing chats).
- Handshake timing change improved sys CPU but exposed NIC-triggered jitter on some hardware. The fixed microsecond value is suboptimal across the fleet.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Diego: Prototype cohort-based TTL for KV cache (short/medium/long) with heuristics based on session length and recent reuse. Measure hit rate and memory. ETA: 2027-03-18.
- Liam: Implement lock-scope reduction patch for kernel scheduler freelist and run microbenchmarks. Open PR and link to JIRA INF-4267. ETA: 2027-03-16.
- Sofia: Add adaptive-handshake experiment that sets handshake backoff proportional to NIC load and CPU steal. Roll out as canary config flag. ETA: 2027-03-15.
- Priya + Maya: Run a focused shadow test with higher proportion of long-context traffic to validate cohort-TTL behaviour. Schedule window: 2027-03-14 -> 2027-03-16.
- Oncall: Add an alert for eviction-rate > 1.2%/min for 10m sustained on any serving pool (threshold bump is temporary while we iterate).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we gate gentle-batcher ramp-window changes by route type (chat vs single-shot)? Could be a quick win but increases config surface.
- How do we identify pinned contexts reliably without adding heavy instrumentation? Session-id heuristics are noisy.
- Is the kernel handshake a workload-dependent tuning knob that should be per-node-type? If so, we need a stable naming + rollout plan.

Risks noted:
- Cohort TTL increases complexity in eviction code — more edge cases and potential regressions. Need robust unit tests + property tests.
- Per-route gating will require updates to rollout and the console; must coordinate with product-hosted-api.

Next summit / sync:
- Quick follow-up on 2027-03-15 for initial adaptive-handshake results.
- Full review of cohort-TTL experiment and microkernel lock PR on 2027-03-18.

Misc notes / tangents captured:
- Paul suggested a lightweight telemetry tag for "kv-pin-candidate" flagged at request origination based on session age > 2m and reuse > 3. Capture as a trace tag for now.
- Priya to add a short dashboard: "gentle-batcher health" (p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, eviction-rate) and expose as per-route chart in Console.

Raw links and artifacts (re-iterated):
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289 (gentle-batcher config globals)
- JIRA: INF-4267 (kernel scheduler lock scope)
- Confluence notes: /spaces/SERV/pages/7921-Gentle-Batcher-Design-Notes

If anyone sees an important omission in these notes, ping me (Maya) or drop edits directly to the doc. I want to keep this as the working capture while we iterate on the three parallel workstreams.

-- Maya
